note: Both arms read one recipe file -- GYM's vendored HowToCook-mcp keeps it at build/data/all_recipes.json, the MCP server imports it and mirage's `cook` CLI is pointed at the same path -- so this compares two clients over one corpus rather than two copies of it. The MCP server answers with a JSON document as text; the CLI prints the same JSON.

cases.name: corpus_size
cases.why: both arms see the same 322 dishes, which is the pool the menu is chosen from

cases.name: category_membership
cases.why: the same category holds the same dishes, so a course picked by browsing one is pickable by browsing the other

cases.name: recipe_ingredients
cases.why: the same dish has the same ingredient list, which is what both deliverables are counted from
